tips.text: "Awareness without change is just self-observation." (you, Ch. 1)
The one version of yourself you fear is the one who stopped caring. Check which one is typing.
Money is the floor, not the ceiling.
Content, or hiding in contentment? You don't always know in the moment. Ask anyway.
Same person watched or not, just louder alone.
Rain, park nights, an absolutely ass dinner. You love the mundane. You said so.
Four months after the fog, you were the one handing out lanterns.
Sol: "It's not what people say, it's the questions they ask." (your dad)
Sol: a question you carry a long time is sometimes the point, not the answer.
Persi: okay. What are we actually doing today?
Persi: say it out loud. That's how you make it real.
Vera: the planning can be the comfortable version of the studying.
Vera: your worry tracks contact, not exposure. Check on the quiet things.
Vex: what would have to be true for this to work, and is it?
Artis: the form shows up when you've lived enough to fill it.
Crow: the sharpness and the warmth are one faculty, not two.
Crow: completion, not regret.
"You must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool." (Feynman)
"It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live." (Marcus Aurelius)
"If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it." (Marcus Aurelius)
"If a man does not know to which port he is steering, no wind is favourable to him." (Seneca)
"The things we have to learn before we can do them, we learn by doing them." (Aristotle)
"When you know a thing, hold that you know it; when you do not, allow that you do not." (Confucius)
"Love in action is a harsh and dreadful thing compared with love in dreams." (Zosima)
"Above all, don't lie to yourself." (Dostoevsky)
"No man ever steps in the same river twice." (Heraclitus)
"All that is mine I carry with me." (Stilbo, via Seneca)
"Err and err and err again, but less and less and less." (Piet Hein)
"A theory that explains everything explains nothing." (Popper)
"Rest is not idleness." (John Lubbock)
